title: ci(test-shards): widen Test Core from 6 to 8 shards
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DWDhLxhv4cQX1gMYwSzVYWk)_

Fixes #25376

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Test Core goes from 6 to 8 shards. It was sized on a fresh merge-group timing table on current `main`, as the 2026-10-23T19:55Z unlock asked, not on the card's 2026-10-13 arithmetic. Eight shards cut the slowest shard by 10–15% on every replay below, so this clears the ~10% bar. The Test Core timeout moves 50 → 60, because the stall-guard headroom tool shows 50 is already too short at six.

## Step 1: the timing table this is sized from

**Merge-group run [40155484566](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/40155484566)** (PR #25730's queue build, head `c882092b33` on `main` `ec4ef94ead`, 2026-10-25 02:42Z). 59 packages were executed and 1 replayed (`@objectstack/spec`); the CLI ran as its 3 slices. Read from the `Test Core` aggregator's timing table and suite-ceiling list, and from each shard's `shard-timing-drift` line:

| shard | predicted bin | measured test windows | `Run this shard's tests` step |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| 1/6 | 809.4 s executed + spec (replayed, 1606.6 s) | 929.5 s | 666 s |
| 2/6 | 2416.5 s | 3211.4 s | 1043 s |
| 3/6 (CLI slice) | 2412.5 s | 2136.6 s | 1387 s |
| 4/6 (CLI slice) | 2419.2 s | 3109.2 s | **1794 s** |
| 5/6 (CLI slice) | 2419.5 s | 2661.2 s | 1498 s |
| 6/6 | 2414.5 s | 2368.7 s | 989 s |

Heaviest packages on that run, measured vs pinned: `cli` 3036.30 s vs 2899.02 s (all 3 slices, ~1012 s each), `objectql` 1044.70 vs 970.12, `runtime` 936.14 vs 848.96, `plugin-auth` 789.01 vs 405.25, `rest` 735.83 vs 876.56, `plugin-security` 666.28 vs 360.02. Spec's heaviest repo files after #25372: `build-schemas-check-mode.git-topology` 432.88 s, `.deleted-baseline` 403.48 s, `.deletion-proofs` 377.06 s.

A smaller merge-group run on the same day, [40157571602](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/40157571602) (21 packages executed; core, spec and types replayed), had its slowest step at 1381 s on the shard holding a CLI slice.

## Step 2: 6 vs 8, predicted

Bins are not wall time. On a shard, the whole packages run four at a time, and a CLI slice then runs as a serial leg of its own. So a shard's tests step reads close to `wholeSum / 2.9 + slice`. On run 40155484566 this model lands within 6.1% of the measured step on the four slowest shards (the three slice shards and shard 2). It misreads the two light shards, which never set the wall. Each list below is replayed through the partitioner's own `planRun()` at each count:

| list | slowest shard at 6 | slowest shard at 8 | change |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| run 40155484566 (60 packages) | ~1696 s (measured 1794 s) | ~1436 s | **−15%** |
| full dataset list (75 packages) | ~1491 s | ~1277 s | −14% |
| run 40157571602 (24 packages) | ~1080 s (measured 1381 s) | ~967 s | −10% |

The partitioner's own bins on the committed dataset (the CLI as 3 slices; `ratio` = max/mean):

```
 6 shards -> max 2489s  mean 2488s  ratio 1.00x
 7 shards -> max 2136s  mean 2133s  ratio 1.00x
 8 shards -> max 1868s  mean 1866s  ratio 1.00x
 9 shards -> max 1661s  mean 1659s  ratio 1.00x
10 shards -> max 1607s  mean 1493s  ratio 1.08x   <- spec's whole weight is the floor
```

**What eight cannot move:** a CLI slice runs serially for about 960–1010 s. On small runs at eight, the slice shards carry almost nothing else, so that is where the −10% stops. A ninth shard would mostly add a runner. The `1.3×` balance bound is unchanged and still met: spec's 1607 s floor sits against `1.3 × 1866 = 2426 s`. Pin 3c (CLI n = 3) is independent of the shard count and still holds.

**Cost:** over the window below, job start → tests step is 1.6 min median (5.5 min p90), and the tail after the step is 0.2 min. Two more shards cost about +3.6 runner-min per run at the median. The card's maintainer directive accepts this.

## Step 3: the timeout, re-derived

`node scripts/measure-stall-guard-headroom.mjs` covered the 89 completed, non-cancelled CI runs created 2026-10-24 03:00Z → 2026-10-25 03:45Z (23 merge_group, 39 pull_request, 16 push, 11 schedule; 512 `Test Core (N/6)` jobs):

```
.github/workflows/ci.yml  job `test`  step `Run this shard's tests`
    W 10m · C 20m · T 50m (job timeout-minutes)
    worst observed: p 2m03s + s 38m24s = 40m27s   (522 observation(s), worst on `Test Core (1/6)`)
    undeferred  p+s+W = 50m27s vs T 50m  ->  UNCOVERED by 0m27s
    deferred    p+s+C = 60m27s vs T 50m  ->  UNCOVERED by 10m27s
```

So 50 is already short at six. The worst case is a red PR shard (run 40149547507). The healthy worst is 37m22s (p 7m28s + s 29m54s, run 40125226571 `Test Core (4/6)`, job wall 37m41s). Scaled to eight by 0.90, the smallest gain above (the safe side):

| reading | at eight | needs |
| :-- | --: | --: |
| window verdict, p + s + 10m | 2m03s + 34m34s + 10m = 46m37s | > 46.6 |
| cap-deferred verdict, p + s + 20m | 56m37s | > 56.6 |
| 80% wall margin, healthy worst wall | ~34m40s | ≥ 43.3 |
| #16465 red line, slowest shard ≤ 70% of timeout | ~34m40s | ≥ 49.5 |
| drift ceiling, healthy worst step at 1.5× prediction | 7m28s + 26m55s × 1.5 = 47.8m | > 47.8 |

The largest reading wins, as in the #22075 derivation: **60** (3m23s over the deferred path). The revert condition in `ci.yml` now reads "below 60". The first full-battery run after landing re-takes these readings on eight-shard jobs.

## What changed

- `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs`: `SHARD_COUNT` 6 → 8. Its header now carries the 6-vs-8 arithmetic above. The "#10472 asked for 6 → 8 and the answer was no" paragraph is rewritten (kept, not deleted) to say why the answer changed.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, Test Core:
  - the matrix is `1..8`;
  - `name: Test Core (… /8)`, `--shard …/8`, the remote-cache and prune `--site` labels, the drift `--label`, `--total 8`, and the `-of-8` artifact names;
  - the aggregator's `--leg "test/8:…"`;
  - `timeout-minutes: 60`;
  - the "WHY SIX" comment block is rewritten as "WHY EIGHT" / "WHY NOT MORE THAN EIGHT" with today's numbers, and the history paragraphs are kept.
- `scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs`: `SHARD_COUNT` 6 → 8, now only its matchers' default. Since the second commit, a candidate run is judged at **its own width**: `runShardWidth` reads `M` from the run's `Test Core (N/M)` job names, and the run is admitted when all `M` shards concluded success and all `M` `-of-M` summaries are retained. A run whose Test Core jobs disagree on `M`, or that has none, is refused by name. Each candidate carries `shard_count` beside its `artifact_ids`.
- `.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml`: the summary download loop and the PR body's per-shard line read the shard roster from the selector's `artifact_ids` instead of spelling `1 2 3 4 5 6`. The selector only admits a run when all of that run's shards are present, so those keys are that run's roster, whatever its width. Wording that said "six" now names the count generically.
- `scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs`: the fixtures that edit the live `ci.yml` (grow the matrix, shrink the roster, the name variants) use the 8-shard spellings. The replays of measured six-shard runs (38036705318, 34007386254) read the live workflow with the six-shard name, and that substitution is asserted. The live-name pin now checks `Test Core (1..8/8)`.
- `scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs`: the live-specimen battery follows the `/8` name.
- `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs`: four `-of-6` spellings in comments and output text now name the width generically (`-of-<width>`, `N-of-M`), since a refresh window can mix widths.

Historical run fixtures elsewhere (`scripts/pm/*`, merge-queue triage) keep the `(N/6)` names their runs really had.

**No refresh transition window.** The first head of this PR judged every candidate at the live count, so `Regenerate the shard-timings dataset` rejected all 24 recent schedule runs (each a whole, green 6-shard run) as missing `7/8`, `8/8`, and exited 1 ([job 121075952437](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/40162213660/job/121075952437)). That would have held for every refresh until an 8-shard schedule run existed with its one-day artifacts still retained. The dataset is per package, and the width a run was split at is not an input to any package's weight, so the fix reads each run at its own width rather than reporting NOT MEASURED through the window.

Tests: a new self-test battery, `width change (#25376)` (9 cases: a whole 6-shard run is eligible under the 8-shard matrix; the same run pinned to 8 is rejected as job 121075952437 rejected it; an old-width run missing `6-of-6` or with `6/6` cancelled is refused; 6 jobs with `-of-8` summaries is refused; jobs disagreeing on `M` and a run with no Test Core job are refused by name; an unanchored `Test Core (3/8) rerun` does not move the width; `listCandidates` reports an 8-wide and a 6-wide run each with its own width). The accumulation battery gains a leg that drives the refresh workflow's real generate step over one 8-wide and two 6-wide runs, with a package measured only in each run's last shard. Both were checked to fail against the old reading: restoring the fixed-width default fails the first case, and restoring a fixed `1..8` download loop fails the accumulation leg.

**Serial with #25697 / PR #25738:** #25738 landed first (`c61f75d`); this branch merges it in, with no conflict.

## Acceptance (from the card)

- Partition self-test, `check-aggregator-roster`, `check:ci-filter-parity` green locally (below) and on this PR.
- After landing, reported on #25376: the first full-battery run's slowest `Test Core` tests step, and max shard wall / timeout (≤ 70%, #16465).

## Local verification (head `8c254ff`)

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (70 families) and reconciled with `--ran`: **66 exit 0, 4 NOT MEASURED**.

- NOT MEASURED (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, they read built `dist/` and this worktree has no full build; CI runs them): `pnpm check:dts-closure`, `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure`, `pnpm check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`.
- Among the green ones: `node scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs --self-test` (75 measured packages → 77 items, 8 shards, max/mean 1.00x, bins 1865.66–1867.52 s within the 2899.02 s density cap, CLI ×3), `node scripts/check-aggregator-roster.mjs` and `--self-test`, `node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` and `--self-test`, `pnpm check:shard-attestation`, `pnpm check:required-contexts`, `pnpm check:pm-expected-skips`, `pnpm check:stall-guard-budget`, `pnpm check:stall-guard-headroom`, `node scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs --self-test` (it executes the refresh workflow's generate step, so the new roster loop ran), `node scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs --self-test`.
- `node scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD`: OK.
